definitions.explanation: Hands without gloves, tools, or weapons. Emphasizes doing something with nothing but one's own hands.

examples.japanese: {素手|すで}で{触|さわ}らないでください。
examples.english: Please don't touch it with your bare hands.

examples.japanese: {素手|すで}で{魚|さかな}をつかんだ。
examples.english: I grabbed the fish with my bare hands.

examples.japanese: {薬品|やくひん}を{扱|あつか}うときは{素手|すで}ではなく{手袋|てぶくろ}を{使|つか}ってください。
examples.english: When handling chemicals, use gloves instead of bare hands.

notes:
USAGE:
Used adverbially with で: {素手|すで}で (with bare hands). Implies doing something without the protection or assistance of tools, gloves, or weapons. In martial arts, {素手|すで} means fighting without weapons (unarmed).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {素手|すで}で{触|さわ}る: to touch with bare hands
- {素手|すで}で{戦|たたか}う: to fight bare-handed
- {素手|すで}でつかむ: to grab with bare hands
- {素手|すで}で{料理|りょうり}する: to cook with bare hands

SIMILAR WORDS:
{手|て}ぶら (empty-handed) means arriving without bringing anything, while {素手|すで} specifically means bare hands without gloves or tools.
